title.en: Gordon Moore: The Forecast That Became a Law
title.zh: 戈登·摩尔：一条被当成定律的预测

dek.en: A four-page magazine article from 1965 set the rhythm of the whole chip industry for decades.
dek.zh: 1965 年一篇四页的文章，给整个芯片业定下了几十年的节奏

social.en: The forecast the chip industry chased for 60 years
social.zh: 芯片业追了六十年的一条预测

igHook.zh:

seoTitle.en: Gordon Moore and Moore's Law: What He Predicted in 1965 and Why It Came True
seoTitle.zh: 戈登·摩尔与摩尔定律：1965 年的预测是什么，为什么会成真

seoDesc.en: What is Moore's Law? In April 1965 Gordon Moore, then at Fairchild, predicted in Electronics magazine that chips would hold 65,000 components by 1975. He co-founded Intel in 1968, revised the forecast to a doubling every two years in 1975, and later said it was "not a law in any real respect". How a forecast about cost became the industry's schedule, from the Intel 4004's 2,300 transistors to 208 billion today, with every fact sourced.
seoDesc.zh: 摩尔定律是什么？1965 年 4 月，在仙童半导体工作的戈登·摩尔在《电子学》杂志上预测，到 1975 年一块芯片能放 6.5 万个元件。1975 年他改为每两年翻一番，他也是英特尔的联合创始人，后来却说这"根本不算什么定律"。一条关于成本的预测，怎样变成整个行业的时间表，从英特尔 4004 的 2300 个晶体管到今天的 2080 亿个，每个事实附来源。

keywords: Cramming more components onto integrated circuits

caption.en: A 12-inch silicon wafer. Each small rectangle is one chip; cramming more of them onto each wafer, and more components onto each chip, is what Moore's forecast was about.
caption.zh: 一片 12 英寸硅晶圆，上面每个小方块就是一颗芯片。在晶圆上放更多芯片、在芯片上放更多元件，正是摩尔那条预测讲的事。

alt.en: A round silicon wafer covered in a grid of chips, shimmering in rainbow colours
alt.zh: 布满芯片方格、泛着彩虹光泽的圆形硅晶圆

lede.en: In April 1965 the magazine Electronics ran an article by a chemist who headed research and development at Fairchild Semiconductor. Gordon Moore had plotted how many components chipmakers could fit on one chip at the lowest cost, drawn a line through just five data points, and extended it ten years: "by 1975, the number of components per integrated circuit for minimum cost will be 65,000" [[1]][[4]]. In 1975 a new memory chip held 65,536 [[8]].
lede.zh: 1965 年 4 月，《电子学》（Electronics）杂志刊登了一篇文章，作者是化学家、仙童半导体的研发负责人戈登·摩尔。他把芯片厂商在成本最低时能在一块芯片上放多少个元件画成图，只用五个数据点连成一条线，再往后延长十年："到 1975 年，成本最低的集成电路上的元件数将达到 65000 个" [[1]][[4]]。1975 年，一款新的存储芯片恰好装下了 65536 个 [[8]]。

lede.en: The line kept going. Intel's first microprocessor, in 1971, had 2,300 transistors [[11]]; Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs have 208 billion [[13]]. The forecast got a name, Moore's Law, and for decades the industry planned around it. Yet Moore himself said: "It's not a law in any real respect. It was an observation and a projection" [[5]]. So why did it come true?
lede.zh: 这条线一直延伸了下去。1971 年，英特尔第一颗微处理器有 2300 个晶体管 [[11]]；今天英伟达的 Blackwell GPU 有 2080 亿个 [[13]]。这条预测有了名字，叫摩尔定律，几十年里整个行业都按它来做计划。可摩尔自己说："它根本不算什么定律，只是一个观察和一个推测" [[5]]。那它为什么成真了？

h.en: Start here: what does doubling mean?
h.zh: 先看懂：翻一番意味着什么

paras.en: A chip is a small slab of silicon carrying tiny electronic parts: transistors, which act as switches, and in 1965 also resistors and other components, wired together on the chip itself [[6]]. Moore's question was how many of those parts a chip could hold before each extra one started to cost more instead of less [[1]].
paras.zh: 芯片是一小块硅片，上面载着微小的电子元件：充当开关的晶体管，以及在 1965 年还很常见的电阻等其他元件，它们在芯片上直接连在一起 [[6]]。摩尔关心的是：一块芯片最多能放多少个元件，再多放一个，每个元件的成本就不降反升 [[1]]。

paras.en: Doubling sounds modest. It is not. In our own arithmetic, doubling every two years for 50 years multiplies a number by more than 33 million. That is roughly the distance between 2,300 transistors and tens of billions.
paras.zh: 翻一番听起来不多，其实很惊人。按我们自己的计算，每两年翻一番，50 年后就是原来的 3300 多万倍。这差不多就是从 2300 个晶体管到几百亿个的距离。

h.en: A forecast about price, not size
h.zh: 一条关于价钱、而不是大小的预测

photo.file: Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce at Intel in 1970.png

caption.en: Gordon Moore (left) and Robert Noyce at Intel in 1970, two years after they founded the company.
caption.zh: 1970 年，戈登·摩尔（左）和罗伯特·诺伊斯在英特尔，那时他们创办公司已经两年。

alt.en: Black-and-white photo of two men in shirts and ties looking at papers
alt.zh: 两位穿衬衫打领带的男士看着文件的黑白照片

paras.en: The article, "Cramming more components onto integrated circuits", appeared on 19 April 1965 [[1]][[3]]. It opens: "The future of integrated electronics is the future of electronics itself" [[2]]. Its point was economic. "Reduced cost is one of the big attractions of integrated electronics," Moore wrote, and he observed that the number of components at the lowest cost per component had "increased at a rate of roughly a factor of two per year" [[1]].
paras.zh: 这篇文章题为《把更多元件塞进集成电路》（Cramming more components onto integrated circuits），刊于 1965 年 4 月 19 日 [[1]][[3]]。开头一句是："集成电子的未来，就是电子业本身的未来" [[2]]。它讲的是经济账。摩尔写道："成本降低是集成电子的一大吸引力"，他还观察到，在每个元件成本最低时，芯片上的元件数"大约每年翻一番" [[1]]。

paras.en: He also guessed what cheap chips would bring: "such wonders as home computers", "automatic controls for automobiles, and personal portable communications equipment" [[1]]. Looking back, he said: "My original message was to get the idea across that integrated circuits were going to be cheap someday" [[7]]. At the time, he said, "I thought I was just showing a local trend" [[5]].
paras.zh: 他还猜测了便宜的芯片会带来什么："家用电脑这样的奇迹"，"汽车的自动控制，以及个人便携通信设备" [[1]]。多年后他回顾说："我最初想说的，是集成电路总有一天会变得便宜" [[7]]。他还说，写那篇文章时，"我以为自己只是在描述一个局部的趋势" [[5]]。

h.en: 1975: every two years, and a name he could not say
h.zh: 1975 年：改成两年，和一个他说不出口的名字

paras.en: Ten years later Moore, by then at Intel, revised the pace at the IEEE International Electron Devices Meeting: "a doubling every two years, rather than every year" [[3]][[4]]. The name came from someone else. The engineer Carver Mead is widely credited with calling it Moore's Law, though when the term was first used is unclear [[6]][[3]].
paras.zh: 十年后，已在英特尔的摩尔在 IEEE 国际电子器件会议上修正了速度："每两年翻一番，而不是每年" [[3]][[4]]。"定律"这个名字来自别人。人们普遍认为是工程师卡弗·米德（Carver Mead）把它叫作摩尔定律，不过这个说法最早出现在什么时候并不清楚 [[6]][[3]]。

paras.en: Moore was uneasy with it. For a long time, he said, he "couldn't even utter the term" [[5]]. Intel itself describes the principle as "an operating principle and commitment rather than a force of nature" [[8]].
paras.zh: 摩尔对这个名字并不自在。他说，很长一段时间里他"连这个词都说不出口" [[5]]。英特尔自己也把它描述为"一种运营原则和承诺，而不是自然规律" [[8]]。

h.en: The turn: from a record to a target

paras.en: Here is the counter-intuitive part. A law of nature holds whether or not anyone believes it. Moore's Law held largely because the industry believed it. "Then it became a self-fulfilling prophecy," Moore said. "The industry recognized it had to stay on that rate of progress or fall behind" [[7]]. The historian Cyrus Mody makes the same point: the idea "has long been a coordinating concept and common goal" for chipmakers [[6]].
paras.zh: 反常识的地方就在这里。自然规律不管有没有人信都成立；摩尔定律之所以成立，很大程度上是因为整个行业信了它。摩尔说："后来它变成了一个自我实现的预言。行业意识到，必须跟上这个速度，否则就会落后" [[7]]。历史学家赛勒斯·莫迪（Cyrus Mody）也这样看：这个想法"长期以来是芯片业的协调概念和共同目标" [[6]]。

paras.en: Chipmakers, equipment makers and chip designers could all plan around the same schedule, each expecting the others to deliver on time. Moore came to accept the name as it "became something that almost drove the semiconductor industry rather than just recording its progress" [[5]]. By 2010 commercial microprocessors had passed a billion transistors [[4]].
paras.zh: 芯片制造商、设备商和芯片设计公司都按同一张时间表做计划，每一方都预期其他方会按时交付。摩尔后来也接受了这个名字，因为它"几乎变成了推动半导体行业的力量，而不只是记录它的进步" [[5]]。到 2010 年，商用微处理器的晶体管数已经超过 10 亿个 [[4]]。

h.en: He also built the companies that kept the pace
h.zh: 他也创办了跟上这个节奏的公司

caption.en: An Intel C4004, Intel's first microprocessor (1971), with 2,300 transistors.
caption.zh: 英特尔 C4004，英特尔第一颗微处理器（1971 年），有 2300 个晶体管。

alt.en: A small white and gold chip with gold pins
alt.zh: 带金色引脚的白色和金色小芯片

paras.en: Moore was not only an observer. In 1957 he was one of eight colleagues who left Shockley Semiconductor to found Fairchild Semiconductor, and in July 1968 he and Robert Noyce founded Intel [[10]]. Intel's 4004, launched in November 1971 for a Japanese calculator maker, put a whole processor on one chip with 2,300 transistors [[11]].
paras.zh: 摩尔不只是旁观者。1957 年，他是离开肖克利半导体、创办仙童半导体的八位同事之一；1968 年 7 月，他和罗伯特·诺伊斯创办了英特尔 [[10]]。英特尔 1971 年 11 月为一家日本计算器公司推出的 4004，把一整个处理器做在一块芯片上，用了 2300 个晶体管 [[11]]。

paras.en: He became Intel's president and chief executive in 1975 and chairman and CEO in 1979, stayed CEO until 1987, and became chairman emeritus in 1997 [[9]]. He received the US National Medal of Technology in 1990 and the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2002 [[9]].
paras.zh: 他 1975 年出任英特尔总裁兼 CEO，1979 年任董事长兼 CEO，CEO 一直做到 1987 年，1997 年成为荣誉董事长 [[9]]。他在 1990 年获美国国家技术奖章，2002 年获总统自由勋章 [[9]]。

caption.en: Gordon Moore at his desk in Intel's Robert Noyce Building, Santa Clara, July 2003.
caption.zh: 2003 年 7 月，戈登·摩尔在英特尔圣克拉拉罗伯特·诺伊斯大楼的办公位上。

alt.en: An older man in a blue shirt sitting in an office cubicle
alt.zh: 穿蓝衬衫的老人坐在办公格子间里

paras.en: In September 2022 Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, said: "Moore's law is dead," adding that "the idea that the chip is going to go down in cost over time, unfortunately, is a story of the past" [[14]]. In March 2024 Nvidia's Blackwell joined two dies, each as large as chipmaking tools can print, into one GPU of 208 billion transistors [[13]]. The count still rises; it is the falling cost, the part Moore cared about most, that is in question.
paras.zh: 2022 年 9 月，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋说："摩尔定律已经死了"，并说"芯片会随着时间越来越便宜，这种想法很遗憾已经成为过去" [[14]]。2024 年 3 月，英伟达的 Blackwell 把两块芯片拼成一颗 GPU，每块都大到制造设备能印出的极限，共有 2080 亿个晶体管 [[13]]。晶体管数量还在增长；成问题的，是成本下降这一部分，也正是摩尔最看重的那部分。

paras.en: The schedule has not stopped either. TSMC, the subject of our previous issue, began high-volume production of its 2-nanometre chips in late 2025 and plans volume production of its A14 process in 2028 [[15]].
paras.zh: 时间表也没有停下。我们上一期写的台积电，2025 年底开始大规模量产 2 纳米芯片，并计划在 2028 年量产 A14 工艺 [[15]]。

paras.en: So why did a line through five dots come true? In our view, because it stopped being only a prediction. Moore offered an observation and a projection; an industry turned it into a promise that each company made to the others, and kept for decades. "I never expected it to be an accurate prediction," Moore said [[7]]. It was accurate because so many people worked to make it so.
paras.zh: 那么，一条只连了五个点的线，为什么会成真？在我们看来，是因为它不再只是一个预测。摩尔给出的是一个观察和一个推测；整个行业把它变成了公司之间彼此的承诺，并守了几十年。摩尔说："我从没指望它是个准确的预测" [[7]]。它之所以准，是因为有太多人在努力让它变准。

a.zh: 不是。摩尔说："只是一个观察和一个推测。"

a.en: The industry made it a target: keep up, or fall behind.
